comments: Adopted distance after a +0.07+/-0.03 mag metallicity correction. Table 13 gives a statistical error from the dereddened PL fit and O/H measurement; no per-galaxy systematic or total error is tabulated.
STR04 nonlinear, long-period LMC PL solution. The quoted uncertainty is random only, and no individual systematic or total modulus error is reported.
STR04 linear LMC PL solution with metallicity correction. Random error only is attached to the modulus; systematic sources are discussed in the H0 error budget.
KN04 nonlinear, long-period LMC PL solution. Metallicity is corrected and the tabulated uncertainty is random only; no module-specific e_S or e_T is given.
KN04 linear LMC PL solution with metallicity correction. A roughly 0.03 mag form-of-PL systematic is discussed, but Table 1 assigns only a random error to the modulus.
TR02 linear LMC PL solution. The tabulated error is random only. Linear fits carry an additional approximately 0.03 mag form-of-PL systematic, but no module-specific e_S or e_T is quoted.
KN06 linear LMC PL solution, used in the authors' preferred linear calibration of H0. Metallicity is corrected; the modulus uncertainty is random only.
KN06 nonlinear, long-period LMC PL solution, preferred for the final nonlinear H0 result. The quoted modulus error is random only.
TR02 nonlinear, long-period LMC PL solution. The metallicity-corrected modulus has random error only; the additional 0.03 mag linearity systematic does not apply.
Pure theoretical F160W PL fit for Z=0.02, Y=0.28 and P>10 d. The 69 good Cepheids define the fit; sigma=0.32 mag. Crowding may explain their anomalously bright and blue distribution.
